records.title: Oropouche virus disrupts neurodevelopment and exhibits congenital infection potential.
records.abstract: Oropouche virus (OROV) historically caused a self-limiting disease, yet recent strains have been clinically linked to congenital infection and neurodevelopmental disease. These observations highlight the need to study OROV as a congenital pathogen. Here, using both a historical and currently circulating strain, we show OROV infects neurons across differentiation states in human forebrain organoids. Compared with the neurotropic congenital pathogen Zika virus (ZIKV), OROV exhibits a heightened capacity for neuroinfection and pathology in both forebrain organoids and neonatal mice. The increased permissiveness of OROV is driven, in part, by a broader neuronal tropism and a relative insensitivity to neuronal type I interferon-mediated antiviral responses. Consistent with clinical observations, neonatal neuroinfection results in rapid and severe neuropathology marked by cerebral hemorrhage. Finally, using a transient type I interferon-blockade model, we demonstrate that OROV can productively infect the murine placenta and cause fetal growth restriction. Together, our complementary models support a unified framework in which placental and fetal barriers limit productive fetal brain infection, yet OROV exhibits marked neurotropism and neuropathogenic potential upon gaining access to developing neural tissues. These findings reinforce the need for vigilant monitoring of OROV as an emerging pathogen associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and congenital disease.

records.title: Generating protein hydrogels with customizable stress relaxation behavior via deep learning-driven entanglement design.
records.abstract: Protein hydrogels are promising artificial extracellular matrices (ECMs) for 3D stem cell and organoid culture due to their favorable stress relaxation behavior (a decrease in stress in response to strain). Inter-chain entangled motifs, in which different protein chains are interlaced, represent a powerful strategy to synthesize such hydrogels. However, designing these motifs with tailored properties such as binding energy remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of simultaneously controlling these properties while ensuring entanglement. Here, we introduce TangleDiff, a deep learning framework for the de novo design of homodimeric entangled proteins with programmable features. TangleDiff generates diverse foldable entangled sequences with an in-silico success rate exceeding 70%, markedly outperforming current models (~1%). By conditioning TangleDiff on inter-chain binding energy, we generate novel protein dimers whose binding energies closely match the specified ranges, with approximately 70% of successful designs conforming to expected values. We experimentally validate TangleDiff by designing nine homodimers targeting various binding energies; seven successfully form hydrogels, with stress relaxation dynamics correlated with specified binding energies. This work establishes a general strategy for entangled protein design, opening avenues for entanglement-based biomaterial innovation.

records.title: Automated Spheroid and Organoid Image Analysis from Rule-Based Methods to Deep Learning.
records.abstract: The increased adoption of three-dimensional (3D) cultures in high-content screening has created an analytical bottleneck in image analysis, prompting the development of automated image analysis tools. This review examines the evolution of automated tools for analysing brightfield and phase-contrast images of spheroids and organoids, from semi-automated approaches through classical machine learning pipelines to modern deep learning tools. Each generation is evaluated according to its underlying principles and limitations, especially when applied to heterogeneous datasets. Rule-based tools were introduced to automate the measurement of morphometric parameters established in manual workflows but may not generalise when experimental conditions change. Classical machine learning improved robustness to post-treatment morphologies but requires retraining when imaging conditions change. A range of deep learning architectures that learn directly from datasets has been introduced, partially reducing the retraining burden associated with classical machine learning. No generation supersedes another across all experimental contexts, and tool selection should be guided by the biological endpoint, image conditions, culture morphology, annotation availability and computational resources. Most tools analyse two-dimensional projections of inherently 3D structures, reducing the accuracy of volume estimates for irregular structures. Independent benchmarks demonstrate that tool performance varies across datasets and imaging laboratories. Future tool development should prioritise robustness across imaging conditions, identification of segmentation failure modes and validation on shared datasets.

records.title: Microbiota-Taurine Pathway Links Dietary Fiber to Mucosal Healing.
records.abstract: Dietary fibers modulate host-microbiota interactions. Whether fiber promotes epithelial repair through microbiota-dependent mechanisms remains unclear. We determined how alginate influences colitis recovery and whether the pathway is relevant to ulcerative colitis (UC). We screened fibers in dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced murine colitis and assessed survival, inflammation, barrier function, and epithelial regeneration. Microbiota dependence was evaluated using antibiotics and bacterial supplementation. Metabolites were profiled using capillary electrophoresis-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (CE-TOFMS), and epithelial programs were analyzed using RNA-seq and colonic organoid injury assays. Slc6a6-/- and Cyp2c55-/- mice were used to determine mechanistic requirements. Translational relevance was examined in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of UC patients receiving antibiotic-primed fecal microbiota transplantation (A-FMT) followed by alginate or placebo. Clinical outcomes, histology, fecal taurine, and colonic CYP2C18 expression were assessed. Alginate improved DSS colitis recovery, reducing inflammation, restoring barrier integrity, and enhancing crypt proliferation. Alginate enriched taurine-releasing bacteria, including Bacteroides acidifaciens and Ligilactobacillus murinus, and increased intestinal taurine; antibiotic disruption abrogated these effects. Taurine was required for benefit, as alginate failed in Slc6a6-/- mice. Alginate and taurine induced epithelial Cyp2c55, and protection was lost in Cyp2c55-/- mice and organoids. In the clinical trial, the primary endpoint was not met. However, alginate supplementation was associated with biological changes, including fecal taurine levels and colonic CYP2C18 expression, consistent with preclinical mechanisms. Alginate engages a fiber-microbiota-taurine-epithelial signaling pathway that promotes recovery in preclinical models. The clinical trial did not meet its primary endpoint; however, the biological changes warrant further investigation of alginate as a microbiota-targeted intervention. jRCTs031200103 (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/), registered September 1, 2020: UMIN000041968 (https://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/index.htm), October 1, 2020.

records.title: Navigating the landscape of stem cell therapeutics: Overcoming translational hurdles via emerging technologies and regulatory frontiers.
records.abstract: Global population aging has increased the incidence of intractable diseases. Accordingly, regenerative medicine using stem cell therapies offers a critical shift from symptom management to functional tissue restoration. Hematopoietic, mesenchymal, and pluripotent stem cells (embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells) have shown promising therapeutic potential. However, their clinical translation is constrained by persistent biological, manufacturing, and regulatory hurdles associated with genomic instability, tumorigenic risk, and batch-to-batch heterogeneity. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current stem cell research landscape, highlighting the strategic shift from traditional cell-centric development to a multi-disciplinary and technology-driven approach. Emerging technologies, including three-dimensional organoids, advanced biomaterials, genome editing, and artificial intelligence-integrated automated manufacturing, are actively resolving long-standing translational bottlenecks to ensure scalable, safe, and reproducible clinical implementation. Regulatory approaches differ across major countries; however, the trend toward incorporating patient needs is growing. This has accelerated access to innovative therapies, with ongoing efforts to ensure that these advances do not compromise safety or efficacy. Moving forward, the successful clinical integration of next-generation stem cell therapeutics is likely to be shaped by the synergy between harmonized regulatory requirements and reliable real-world evidence. Collectively, these factors serve to bridge the transition from early patient access to definitive licensing.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language.
records.abstract: Programming biological function-designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks-is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited1-3: they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein-text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks-a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein-and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints.

records.title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts.
records.abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins.1-5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design6-8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts9. The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

records.title: A Simulation-Free Topological Basis for Building Compact Koopman Models of Protein Folding.
records.abstract: Unravelling protein-folding mechanisms and kinetics is a key challenge to biochemical science. The variational approach for Markov processes (VAMP) is a powerful tool to build Markov Models that capture key kinetic and structural information despite the conformational complexity and long time scales associated with protein folding. However, VAMP-based Markov models use data from exhaustive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to construct an underlying basis set describing the "coarse-grained" kinetics; the same MD data can be used to predict transition probabilities between partitioned configuration space, enabling the extraction of folding time scales and mechanism. Here, we propose an alternative strategy for Markov model construction that does not rely on extensive, computationally demanding MD data for configuration space partitioning. Specifically, we show that graph-driven sampling (GDS) can generate a complete "landscape" of intermediate contact-maps linking unfolded and folded protein conformations; importantly, extensive MD simulations are not required in GDS. When combined with a physically intuitive shortest-contact-hop metric to discriminate different intermediate states, GDS mapping of protein-folding configuration space generates a reliable "structurally aware" partitioning for VAMP model construction. To demonstrate this strategy, we show that a GDS-constructed Markov model variationally improves folding time scale estimates for all-atom models of the WW domain protein─and has the additional advantage of easily resolving kinetic traps in the folding landscape that have proven challenging to confirm otherwise. Together, the combination of GDS and VAMP opens a new route toward rapid characterization of protein-folding intermediates and kinetics traps to help address frontier challenges such as protein misfolding, aggregation, and protein design.

records.title: Structure of a sparsely populated chimeric intermediate that facilitates fold-switching of a metamorphic protein.
records.abstract: Metamorphic proteins challenge the single-sequence-structure-function paradigm by switching between distinct folds that often adopt complementary functions. However, the conformational states sampled along the fold-switching pathway have remained elusive because they are transient and unstable. Using multinuclear chemical exchange saturation transfer and relaxation dispersion NMR, combined with chemical shift-based structure determination and protein engineering, we visualized the atomic resolution structure of an "invisible" state of the metamorphic chemokine lymphotactin. This state is a chimera that integrates the secondary and tertiary structure of one fold with the quaternary assembly of the other. Locking lymphotactin into a single conformation abolishes access to this state, supporting its role as an on-pathway intermediate in metamorphosis. The stabilization of such hybrid intermediates is likely to have facilitated the evolution of fold-switching and represents a powerful strategy for protein design.

records.title: Editing Enzymes with Multiscale Metal-Based Components.
records.abstract: Enzymes are powerful natural catalysts distinguished by high efficiency and selectivity. The use of enzymes in the chemical industry can theoretically enable numerous efficient and sustainable reaction pathways. Nevertheless, the application of enzymes is hindered by their narrow catalytic repertoire. Enzymes are readily deactivated under nonnatural environments, and their reaction types are limited. Developing enzymes with new catalytic functions has been a longstanding challenge in the field of biocatalysis. Strategies such as directed evolution and de novo protein design have been very successful in designing new enzymes. However, as both approaches rely on the engineering of amino acid sequences of proteins, they remain constrained and cannot fully meet the growing demand for non-natural biocatalysis. Incorporating abiotic components with enzymes is a powerful tool for editing enzymes to render new catalytic capabilities. Metal-based components possess a broad catalytic repertoire, structural stability, and multifunctionality, making them promising building blocks for enzyme editing. This Account summarizes our contributions over the past decade in editing enzyme catalysts with metal-based components as a scale-dependent evolution, from nanoscale environmental modulation to atom-scale active site redefinition, illustrating how enzyme editing with metal-based components can systematically address non-natural catalytic challenges. A conceptual framework in which enzymes are edited with metal-based components across scales from the nanometer to the atomic dimension is introduced, establishing a logical basis for integrating biocatalysis with abiotic reactivity. At the nanoscale, enzymes are encapsulated in metal-based frameworks to improve the configuration stability, enabling catalysis under non-native and harsh conditions. The robustness of enzymes under extreme pH, high temperature, and organic solvent can be largely enhanced through the regulation of metal-based frameworks. At the sub-nanoscale, metal clusters are embedded within enzyme scaffolds to construct enzyme-metal hybrid catalysts. By integration of enzymatic and chemical catalysis, new non-natural catalytic processes can be established. At the atomic scale, metal atoms are incorporated into the enzyme catalytic pocket, creating new hybrid active sites. The hybrid active site endows an enzyme with capabilities to drive new-to-nature reactions, unlocking an expanded enzyme catalytic space. This work provides a unifying conceptual framework that clarifies how metal-based components can be strategically employed to reprogram enzyme stability, functionality, and reactivity. We hope that the strategies and concepts discussed herein offer comprehensive design principles for biohybrid catalysts and establish a foundation for reprogramming enzymatic function beyond evolutionary limitations.

records.title: Early and accurate detection of ovarian cancer by profiling cell-free mitochondrial DNA fragmentomics in multi-ethnic population.
records.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains highly lethal due to frequent late-stage diagnosis and the challenge of distinguishing malignant from benign adnexal masses (BAM) preoperatively. Reliable non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers remain an unmet clinical need. This multi-center study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic potential of plasma circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) fragmentomics for improving OC management. We developed two machine learning models based on ccf-mtDNA features: an OC Detection (OD) model to distinguishing OC from healthy controls (HC), and a Benign vs. Malignant Differential diagnosis (BMD) model to discriminate OC from BAM. The OD model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.987 in the training cohort and maintained high performance (AUC above 0.979) in internal and external validation cohorts, with 91.67% sensitivity for Stage I OC at 95% specificity. The BMD model demonstrated strong discriminatory power (AUC = 0.982) and generalizability (AUC ranging from 0.961 to 0.980 in four validation cohorts), significantly outperforming serum biomarkers. Remarkably, both models performed robustly in the Chinese minority cohort. These findings establish ccf-mtDNA fragmentomics as a powerful liquid biopsy approach for the early and accurate detection of OC, with significant potential for clinical translation in high-risk populations and differential diagnosis of benign vs. malignant adnexal masses.

records.title: From cytoreduction to precision oncology: evolution of ovarian cancer therapy.
records.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy due to its asymptomatic progression, limited screening modalities, and late-stage diagnosis. Although initial responses to platinum-based chemotherapy are common, recurrence and multidrug resistance are nearly universal, necessitating a shift toward biomarker-guided, precision-based interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on the evolving landscape of ovarian cancer treatment, with emphasis on molecular pathogenesis, histotype-specific vulnerabilities, and advances in therapeutic strategies. Focus is placed on the clinical integration of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-targeting agents, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates, alongside emerging platforms such as liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence-enhanced diagnostics, and histotype-driven targeted therapies. Translational insights from other malignancies were utilized to highlight future directions for ovarian cancer, including dual pathway targeting, immune and epigenetic modulation, and receptor-guided cytotoxic delivery. Collectively, these advances demonstrate how precision oncology is advancing ovarian cancer treatment, with the potential to improve survival outcomes while preserving quality of life.

records.title: Irinotecan Plus Cetuximab Rechallenge Versus Trifluridine/Tipiracil Plus Bevacizumab as Third-Line Treatment in Circulating Tumor DNA-Selected Metastatic Colorectal Cancer (ROMANCE Trial).
records.abstract: In patients with RAS/BRAF wild-type (WT) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) monoclonal antibodies combined with chemotherapy represent an established first-line option and may provide clinically meaningful tumor shrinkage. However, acquired resistance may develop through the emergence of mechanism/s of acquired resistance. After progression to first- and second-line regimens, the prognosis of patients with mCRC remains poor. Available later-line options exhibit a cytostatic activity and are associated with limited objective response rate (ORR). Of note, the dynamic decay of resistant subclones after withdrawal of EGFR blockade supports the rationale to explore anti-EGFR rechallenge therapy. ROMANCE trial is a multicenter, randomized phase II study. Overall, 150 patients with mCRC with circulating tumor RAS/BRAF/EGFR/PIK3CA exon 20/MAP2K1/MET WT and HER2 nonamplified (negative hyperselected tumors) mCRC, at baseline liquid biopsy, will be randomized 1:1 to irinotecan plus cetuximab rechallenge compared with trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab as third-line therapy. The primary endpoint is ORR assessed by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors 1.1 by blinded independent central review; secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, and quality of life. Given the limited ORRs achieved with currently available options after second-line treatment for refractory mCRC, strategies capable of inducing clinically meaningful tumor shrinkage are urgently required. ROMANCE will evaluate whether cetuximab plus irinotecan retreatment can improve ORR compared with standard third-line trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab in patients with circulating tumor DNA-negative hyperselected mCRC and will clarify the role of anti-EGFR rechallenge in the continuum of care of refractory mCRC. This trial is registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT07381764).

records.title: Mitochondrial DNA mediated Kupffer cell activation in the pathogenesis and progression of liver diseases.
records.abstract: The liver serves as a pivotal metabolic and immunological hub, yet its homeostatic equilibrium is highly susceptible to mitochondrial dysfunction. Recent studies have implicated mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) as an important damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) that links mitochondrial injury to sterile hepatic inflammation and KCs (KCs) activation. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the mtDNA mediated KCs across four major hepatic pathologies: Alcohol-associated Liver Disease (ALD), Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD), Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury (IRI), and Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC). We discuss emerging evidence that Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) associated PANoptosis and nerve injury-induced protein 1 (NINJ1) mediated plasma membrane rupture may contribute to inflammatory cell death in severe liver injury, complementing rather than superseding canonical pyroptotic mechanisms. However, the extent to which mtDNA directly activates this axis remains unresolved. Furthermore, we delineate the cell-type-specific dichotomy of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) signaling, which fuels pro-inflammatory storms in KCs via the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway while promoting protective mitophagy in hepatocytes through a STING-independent cGAS-Beclin-1 interaction. In the context of immunometabolism, we also summarize preclinical evidence linking cytidine/uridine monophosphate kinase 2 (CMPK2) dependent mtDNA synthesis to inflammasome activation and mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) acetylation to age-associated mtDNA release during IRI. Finally, we evaluate the clinical translational potential of targeting these molecular hubs and the emergence of cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf-mtDNA) fragmentomics-including 5' end motif analysis and diversity scoring as a transformative liquid biopsy tool for precision diagnosis. Collectively, available evidence positions mtDNA mediated KCs activation as an important, context-dependent contributor to liver disease and a potential therapeutic target, while underscoring the need for cell-specific and human validation.

records.title: Inferring tissue origin from cell-free DNA in metastatic cancer.
records.abstract: A major clinical challenge in metastatic cancer management is determining not only the presence of tumor-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) but also the tissue lineage and organ context reflected by circulating cfDNA signals. CfDNA supports such inference by retaining molecular signatures specific to its tissue-of-origin, including DNA methylation, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), fragmentomic profiles, nucleosome positioning patterns, and histone modifications. This review examines the biological principles underlying cfDNA-based tissue-of-origin determination, the computational frameworks used to interpret these signals, and the key barriers to clinical translation. We additionally compare representative deconvolution and classification strategies, including linear and probabilistic models, machine/deep learning, and single-cell-informed reference approaches. Despite substantial progress, clinical integration remains hindered by low tumor fractions, heterogeneous contributions from multiple tissues, background noise from nonmalignant cell death, and a lack of robust prospective validation. We further emphasize that source estimates in metastatic plasma should be interpreted in the context of mixed tissue contributions, differential shedding, reference design, and model uncertainty, rather than as direct measures of anatomical metastatic burden.

records.title: GSTP1 promoter hypermethylation in prostate cancer detection: current evidence, clinical positioning, and translational gaps.
records.abstract: GSTP1 promoter hypermethylation is one of the most consistently documented molecular alterations in prostate cancer, with high prevalence in malignant tissue and a well-established relationship with transcriptional silencing. However, despite more than two decades of biological and diagnostic investigation, GSTP1-based testing has not acquired a clearly defined stand-alone role in contemporary prostate cancer detection. This narrative review examines why extensive biological evidence has not translated into routine clinical use and where, if anywhere, GSTP1 testing might provide meaningful value within current diagnostic pathways. Evidence from prostate tissue, urine and circulating cell-free DNA is considered alongside the effects of biospecimen selection, preanalytical handling, CpG target selection, assay design and interpretation thresholds. Tissue demonstrates the most reproducible signal and has achieved partial clinical translation through multiplex testing such as ConfirmMDx, whereas urinary and blood-based approaches remain investigational. Recent urinary findings, including in men with moderately elevated PSA, are promising but remain preliminary and have not established incremental value beyond contemporary risk assessment, biomarkers and multiparametric MRI. The translational priority is therefore not to demonstrate again that GSTP1 detects prostate cancer, but to determine whether a standardised assay provides reproducible, nonredundant and clinically actionable information at a defined decision point. Future development should prioritise clearly specified target populations, analytically validated assay configurations, clinically significant prostate cancer as the relevant endpoint, and prospective evaluation against contemporary diagnostic pathways.

records.title: ClinNetDx: a novel explainable ai framework for acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection using multi-modal clinical data.
records.abstract: Early identification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is vital to respond on time; yet, presently existing diagnostic procedures still depend on laboratory knowledge, manual interpretation and many supplementary exams. This paper introduces ClinNetDx, a new hybrid deep learning model for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia prediction that combines a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Deep Neural Network (DNN) and employs structured blood test data and (optional) medical images to support good health and well-being. The proposed methodology includes a tabular-to-spatial transformation that converts numerical clinical measures into 2D representations, enabling a CNN to learn spatial correlations among features from structured medical data. We use advanced pre-processing methods (normalization, imputation, SMOTE) that are robust to class imbalance and missing variables. For interpretability, we use dual explainability: SHAP values to explain feature contributions for numerical data and Grad-CAM visualizations to generate localized heatmaps for image inputs. To make it accessible in a clinical environment, the system is built as a Django-powered web application that provides on-the-fly predictions and an intuitive presentation of findings. The design is flexible and deployed as a RESTful API for interface with medical information systems, mHealth apps and cloud platforms. To demonstrate the promising predictive and generalizing power of the proposed system, it was evaluated on publicly available multi-modal haematological datasets comprising 5,000 structured CBC records, 2,500 ALL smear images, and 2,000 synchronized multi-modal samples using k-fold cross-validation, with confusion matrices and ROC-AUC reported. Experimental assessment shows that ClinNetDx achieves 98.1% classification accuracy, outperforming conventional machine learning and unimodal deep learning models while maintaining strong precision, recall, and ROC-AUC performance. The proposed system combines accurate multi-modal prediction with interpretable decision support, making it a potential option for computer-assisted early diagnosis of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia and for future clinical decision-support applications.
